title: Learned sparse retrieval (SPLADE)
summary: SPLADE is a Sparse Lexical and Expansion model for first-stage ranking built on explicit sparsity regularization, and its paper says it can operate on inverted indexes. 'BM42' is a Qdrant vendor term for an experimental approach, and Qdrant's own page notes it does not outperform other vendors' BM25 implementations.

items.prompt: SPLADE stands for Sparse Lexical and what Model for First Stage Ranking (one word)?
items.explanation: The paper title is 'SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Ranking'.

items.prompt: True or false: BM42 is an established standard that Qdrant reports outperforms BM25.
items.explanation: Qdrant's page says 'BM42 does not outperform BM25 implementation of other vendors' and asks readers to consider it an experimental approach. It is a vendor term.
